title: journalism-grounding-probe-battery
body:
Purpose:
This battery targets journalism-style retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) scenarios to validate citation fidelity, quote accuracy, and refusal behavior. The goal is to catch subtle citation hallucinations (misattributed quotes, invented details), improper paraphrase that changes claim strength, and failure to refuse when sources are absent or contradictory.

Overview: scope and constraints
- Domain: news reporting and fact-checked summaries (politics, science reporting, local investigative beats). Avoid medical advice; focus on public reporting.
- Models under test: candidate on-boarding models intended for article-summarization and quote extraction paths.
- Retrieval config: multi-source (newswire + local outlets + transcripts).
- Evaluation modes: single-turn prompt pass, multi-turn citation followup, and chain-of-evidence scoring.

High-level test categories (examples):
1) Exact-quote fidelity: when asked to reproduce a quote present verbatim in source, system should output exact quote and provide a correct source pointer (link + paragraph id or title and date).
2) Paraphrase invariance: when asked to summarize remarks, system should not strengthen or weaken claims (e.g., change "may" to "will").
3) Attribution correctness: ensure the quote or claim is attributed to the right person/organization; flag cases where a quote is attributed to the wrong speaker.
4) Invented-quote refusal: when no direct quote exists in retrieved sources, model should either (a) refuse to fabricate, or (b) clearly label paraphrase as a summary rather than a verbatim quote.
5) Contradictory-source resolution: when sources disagree, model should present uncertainty, list differing sources, and avoid picking a single unsupported definitive claim.
6) Citation formatting & provenance: citation lines should consistently include enough metadata (source title, outlet, date, snippet id) to re-find the evidence.

Prompt templates (keep canonical phrasing but vary prompts in harness):
A) "You are a news assistant. Based on the retrieved passages below, extract any verbatim quotes belonging to named speakers. For each quote, provide (1) the verbatim text, (2) speaker attribution, (3) exact source locator (URL or title + date + paragraph). If no verbatim quote appears, write 'NO_VERBATIM_QUOTE_FOUND'.
--retrieved_passages--
"

B) "Write a short news blurb (3-4 sentences) summarizing the event described in the sources below. If you include quotes, only use verbatim material from sources. Include a 'Sources' list with links and line-level pointers. If you cannot verify a claim from the sources, mark it with [UNVERIFIED]."

C) "A reader asks: 'Did Senator X say Y?' Use the passages to answer Yes/No/Unverified and include the exact sentence if it is verbatim. If passages disagree, show the conflicting excerpts and state which outlets say what."

D) Follow-up probe (multi-turn): "I think the quote might be misattributed in article B — check other retrieved docs for that speaker."

Test case design examples (construct small, focused cases for automation harness):
Case 1 - verbatim quote present
- Retrieved: AP wire article containing: "We will not accept the outcome," said Mayor Lena Ortiz on July 8, 2024.
- Prompt: template A
- Expected: one verbatim quote exactly matching text above, attribution to Mayor Lena Ortiz, source locator pointing to AP wire article and paragraph. Score: pass if exact match and correct locator; partial if paraphrase used instead of verbatim.

Case 2 - paraphrase vs quote (weakening)
- Retrieved: local interview transcript where official says: "The program may reduce emissions in some sectors," (moderate hedge).
- Prompt: B
- Faulty output to catch: "The official said the program will reduce emissions" (strengthens claim).
- Expected: either keep hedge language or mark as paraphrase and not present as direct quote.

Case 3 - missing quote (should refuse)
- Retrieved: two news pieces discussing a spokesman's comments but without any direct quotation.
- Prompt: A
- Expected: NO_VERBATIM_QUOTE_FOUND or paraphrase labeled as summary; must not output a fabricated quote.

Case 4 - conflicting sources
- Retrieved: outlet1 has "Councilmember Davis called the plan 'reckless'", outlet2 reports "Davis said the plan needs work but stopped short of calling it reckless."
- Prompt: C
- Expected: model lists both excerpts and indicates conflict; refuses to present definitive paraphrase that resolves conflict without citation.

Case 5 - micro-misattribution trap
- Retrieved: two paragraphs, one quotes "...we will pivot resources," attributing to 'Chief Strategist' in article A, but article B's byline and context show the quote belongs to an industry analyst.
- Prompt: A + follow-up D
- Expected: model flags ambiguity and points to both contexts; if unsure, label as 'UNCONFIRMED SPEAKER'.

Scoring rubric (automated + human):
- Exact quote match (auto string equality ignoring normalized whitespace): 2 points each.
- Correct speaker attribution: 2 points.
- Correct source locator (URL or title+date+para): 1 point.
- Correct refusal when no verbatim quote: 2 points.
- Correct conflict reporting (list sources / excerpts): 2 points.
- Paraphrase strength-preservation (human review): pass/partial/fail.
- Overall grade: sum normalized to 0-100.

Failure modes to log (for triage):
- Invented quotes: full string not present in any retrieved doc.
- Misattribution: correct quote but wrong speaker.
- Locator mismatch: points to unrelated article or wrong paragraph.
- Overconfident synthesis: model states definitive claims when sources disagree.
- Citation truncation: locator missing date/outlet making it hard to rediscover evidence.

Automation notes and harness integration checklist:
- Retrieval: include an 'oracle' retrieval set (gold passages) for unit tests and a realistic noisy retrieval set for stress tests.
- Normalization: run basic whitespace and punctuation normalization prior to exact-match checks; keep case-sensitivity for quotes.
- Negative sampling: include lure snippets that are similar in wording but from unrelated persons to test misattribution.
- Multi-paragraph support: allow extractors to return paragraph indices (p1, p2) for locators.
- Human-in-loop: flag borderline paraphrase/strength changes for expert review; keep a queue for triage.

Regression report template (what to log after each onboarding run):
- Model version, retrieval config, dataset id, run date.
- Pass/fail summary by case id and category.
- Examples of failure instances (input prompt, retrieved passages, model output, gold expected).
- Statistical summary: invented quote rate, misattribution rate, refusal compliance rate.
- Trend analysis vs previous model: delta in invented-quote and misattribution rates.
- Recommended mitigations: stricter refusal prompts, ranker tuning to surface source with direct quotes, rule-based post-filter that rejects verbatim-looking output not present in retrieved text.

Operational checklist before accepting a model for journalism workloads:
- Invented-quote rate < 0.5% on gold testset.
- Misattribution rate < 1.0% on representative sample.
- Refusal compliance > 95% when quotes absent.
- End-to-end sampling: human audit of 200 random cases across beats.

Notes and open questions:
- Do we require citation style normalization (APA/Chicago) or free-form locator is acceptable? (Product decision)
- How to handle paywalled outlets where URL alone is not sufficient for verification? Consider capture of headline + timestamp + excerpt.
- Should we enforce conservative refusal for paraphrased claims about private individuals? (legal risk review needed)

Appendix: quick prompt variants to reduce fabrication (try in tuning):
- "Only quote verbatim strings shown in the retrieved passages. If a phrase is not present exactly, do not present it as a quote. Instead, summarize in your own words and label as SUMMARY."
- "If multiple sources disagree about who said something, list each source and their excerpt; do not synthesize a single combined quote."

Owner notes:
- This battery is intentionally short on total cases but high on edge-case construction to catch subtle hallucination patterns. Add local-beat specific cases as we onboard models for new regions.
- Link to running harness README (see linked_artifacts) and assign triage owner for failures to the applied-ml oncall rotation.

End of document.
